questions.stem:
A train moves along a straight horizontal track between two stations $R$ and $S$. Initially the train is at rest at $R$. The train accelerates uniformly at $\frac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ from rest at $R$ until it is moving with speed $15\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. For the next 200 seconds the train maintains a constant speed of $15\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The train then decelerates uniformly at $\frac{1}{4}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ until it comes to rest at $S$.

Find

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the time taken by the train to travel from $R$ to $S$,
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Use of $v=u+at$ to find $t_1$ or $t_2$ (condone sign errors)
A1: $t_1 = 15 \div 0.5 = 30$ (s) OR $t_2 = 15 \div 0.25 = 60$ (A0 if negative)
A1 cso: Total time $= 30+200+60 = 290$ (s), for 290 with no errors seen
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for use of $v = u + at$ or gradient or any other complete method to find a value for $t_1$ or $t_2$ (condone sign errors)

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: complete method to find distance (must have a $\frac{1}{2}$) either by using trapezium rule or by using 2 triangles and a rectangle
A2 ft: distance $= \frac{1}{2}\times 30\times 15 + 200\times 15 + \frac{1}{2}\times 60\times 15$, follow their $t_1$ & $t_2$ (-1 each error)
A1: $=3675$ (m) (3.675 km)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) the average speed of the train during the journey from $R$ to $S$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Ave. speed $= \dfrac{\text{their (b)}}{\text{their (a)}}$
A1: $=\dfrac{3675}{290}$ oe $\mathrm{(m\,s^{-1})}$ (13 or better) (12.6724..)

parts.text:
Two forces $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$ act on a particle at a point $O$. Force $\mathbf{P}$ has magnitude 6 N and force $\mathbf{Q}$ has magnitude 7 N. The angle between the line of action of $\mathbf{P}$ and the line of action of $\mathbf{Q}$ is $120^\circ$, as shown in Figure 1.

The resultant of $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$ is $\mathbf{R}$.

Find

(i) the magnitude of $\mathbf{R}$,

(ii) the angle between the line of action of $\mathbf{R}$ and the line of action of $\mathbf{P}$.
(8)
parts.mark_scheme:
Method 1:
M1A1: Horizontal component $= 6-7\cos 60$ (N)
M1A1: Vertical component (N) $= 7\cos 30$
M1A1: Use Pythagoras: $\sqrt{2.5^2+(7\cos 30)^2}=\sqrt{43}=6.6$(N) or better
M1A1: Use trig: angle $=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{7\cos 30}{2.5}\right)=68^\circ$ (below $\mathbf{P}$) or better. Also allow $112^\circ$, $292^\circ$ or $248^\circ$

Alt (cosine/sine rule method):
M2A2: Cosine rule to find $|\mathbf{R}|$: $R^2 = 36+49-2\times6\times7\times\cos 60 (=43)$
M1A1: $R=6.6$ (N) or better
M1: Solve Sine rule for $\theta$: $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{7\sin 60}{R}\right)$
A1: $=68^\circ$ or better. Also allow $112^\circ$ or $292^\circ$ or $248^\circ$
Notes: First M2 for use of cosine rule with correct structure but allow $\cos 120^\circ$ and allow $R^2$; First A2 for a correct equation (A0 if $120^\circ$ used); Third M1 for solving for $R$; Third A1 for $\sqrt{43}$, 6.6 (N) or better; Fourth M1 for complete method (e.g. sine rule) to find angle between their $\mathbf{R}$ and $\mathbf{P}$; Fourth A1 for $68^\circ$ or better
Official notes (completeness pass):
- First M1 for attempt, allow sin/cos confusion, to find component parallel to $\mathbf{P}$
- First A1 for a correct expression
- Second M1 for attempt, allow sin/cos confusion to find component perp to $\mathbf{P}$
- First A1 for a correct expression
- Third M1 for using Pythag to find magnitude of $\mathbf{R}$
- Fourth M1 for complete method to find angle (M0 if 6 used for 'horiz' cpt)
- Fourth A1 for $68^\circ$ or better (67.589089…) $112^\circ$ or $292^\circ$ or $248^\circ$

questions.stem:
A particle $P$ of mass 4 kg is held at rest at the point $A$ on a rough plane which is inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The point $B$ lies on the line of greatest slope of the plane that passes through $A$. The point $B$ is 5 m down the plane from $A$, as shown in Figure 3. The coefficient of friction between the plane and $P$ is 0.3

The particle is released from rest at $A$ and slides down the plane.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the speed of $P$ at the instant it reaches $B$.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: Resolve perpendicular to plane: $R=4g\cos 30$
B1: $F=0.3R$ seen (could just be on diagram)
M1: Use of $F=ma$ parallel to plane: $4a=4g\sin 30-F$
A1: correct equation ($F$ not substituted)
A1: $4a=4g\sin 30-0.3\times 4g\cos 30$, a correct equation in $a$ only, without trig ratios substituted
M1: Use of $v^2=(u^2+)2as$: $v=\sqrt{10a}$, complete method for finding $v$ (must have found an $a$ value)
A1: $v=4.9$ or 4.85 $(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}})$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- First M1 for equation of motion, with usual rules, condone sign errors

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The particle is now returned to $A$ and is held in equilibrium by a horizontal force of magnitude $H$ newtons, as shown in Figure 4. The line of action of the force lies in the vertical plane containing the line of greatest slope of the plane through $A$. The particle is on the point of moving up the plane.

(b) Find the value of $H$.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1A1: Resolve perpendicular to the plane: $R=4g\cos 30+H\cos 60$
M1A1: Resolve parallel to the plane: $H\cos 30=F+4g\sin 30$
M1: Use of $F=0.3R$ (N.B. M0 if using $R$ from part (a))
DM1: dependent on first, second and third M's, for eliminating $F$ and $R$ and solving for $H$: $H=\dfrac{g(1.2\cos 30+4\sin 30)}{\cos 30-0.3\cos 60}$
A1: $=42$ or 41.6

Alt (6b alt): Resolve vertically: $R\cos 30=4g+F\cos 60$ (M1A1); Resolve horizontally: $H=R\cos 60+F\cos 30$ (M1A1); Use of $F=0.3R$ (M1); Solve for $H$ (DM1); $H=42$ or 41.6 (A1)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- First M1 for a resolution, with usual rules, condone sign errors. First A1 for a correct equation. Second M1 for another resolution, with usual rules, condone sign errors. Second A1 for a correct equation
- N.B. Enter marks on ePen for equations as they appear.

questions.stem: Two particles $P$ and $Q$ have masses 3 kg and $m$ kg respectively ($m>3$). The particles are connected by a light inextensible string which passes over a smooth light fixed pulley. The system is held at rest with the string taut and the hanging parts of the string vertical. The particle $Q$ is at a height of 10.5 m above the horizontal ground, as shown in Figure 5. The system is released from rest and $Q$ moves downwards. In the subsequent motion $P$ does not reach the pulley. After the system is released, the tension in the string is 33.6 N.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ is $1.4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Motion of $P$: $T-3g=3a$
A1: $33.6-3g=3a$
A1: $a=1.4\,(\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}})$ *Given Answer* (units not needed)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for equation of motion for $P$ with $T$ not substituted, condone sign errors. First A1 for a correct equation in $a$ only (allow $\pm a$)

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Motion of $Q$: $mg-T=ma$ (with neither $T$ nor $a$ substituted, condone sign errors)
A1: $mg-33.6=1.4m$, a correct equation in $m$ only
A1: $m=4$
N.B. Whole system equation: $mg-3g=a(m+3)$ may be used

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The system is released from rest at time $t=0$. At time $T_1$ seconds after release, $Q$ strikes the ground and does not rebound. The string goes slack and $P$ continues to move upwards.

(c) Find the value of $T_1$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1A1: Use of $s=ut+\frac{1}{2}at^2$: $10.5=\frac{1}{2}\times1.4\times t^2$
A1: $T_1=\sqrt{15}=3.9$ or better
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for a complete method to find $T_1$ (M0 if $g$ used). First A1 for a correct equation (or equations)
- $v=\sqrt{29.4}$ (5.4) may be found in this part but only gets credit if it appears in part (d)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
At time $T_2$ seconds after release, $P$ comes to instantaneous rest.

(d) Find the value of $T_2$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Use $v^2=(u^2+)2as$ to find speed of particles when $Q$ hits ground: $v=\sqrt{2\times1.4\times10.5}\;(=\sqrt{29.4})$
DM1: dependent, use $v=u+at$ to find additional time for $P$ to come to rest: $0=\sqrt{29.4}-gt$
A1: Total time: $T_2=\sqrt{15}+\dfrac{\sqrt{29.4}}{9.8}=4.4$ or 4.43
Official notes (completeness pass):
- First M1 for a complete method to find the speed of particles when $Q$ hits the ground (M0 if using $g$). Second M1 dependent on first M1 for a complete method to find the additional time for $P$ to come to rest (must be using $g$)

parts.label: e
parts.text:
At time $T_3$ seconds after release ($T_3 > T_1$) the string becomes taut again.

(e) Sketch a velocity-time graph for the motion of $P$ in the interval $0 \leqslant t \leqslant T_3$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: Shape. Graph does not need to go down as far as it goes up and ignore gradients. (B0 if it goes outside the range $0\leqslant t\leqslant T_3$ or if a continuous vertical line is included)
DB1 ft: dependent on first B1, ft on their $\sqrt{29.4}$, $T_1$ and $T_2$, their values for 5.4, -5.4, 3.9, 4.4 (or $T_1$ $T_2$). Allow $T_1$ and $T_2$ entered on the graph (rather than their numerical values)
